core_obligations: The component morphisms (proof lines 1161-1177): in case A, u_n = u_varphi u_0 (independent of varphi : [0] -> [n] by the datum) is a morphism of sites a_n : C_n -> D with a_m f_varphi = a_n; in case B, u_n = u_0 u_varphi is cocontinuous and defines a_n : Sh(C_n) -> Sh(D) with the same compatibilities.

The total morphism a (lines 1179-1216): a^{-1}G is the sheaf on C_total with components a_n^{-1}G and transition maps the canonical identifications f_varphi^{-1}a_m^{-1}G = a_n^{-1}G (sheaves-on-total description); since the a_n^{-1} are exact, a^{-1} is exact; a_*F is defined as the equalizer of a_{0,*}F_0 -> a_{1,*}F_1 (the two maps from varphi : [0] -> [1] through a_{0,*}f_{varphi,*}f_varphi^{-1}F_0 and F(varphi)); a map a^{-1}G -> F is, by the adjunctions for the a_n, a map of cosimplicial sheaves G_bullet -> a_{bullet,*}F, which by the dual of the Simplicial augmentation lemma is a map G -> a_*F; hence a^{-1} and a_* are adjoint and yield the morphism of topoi a (the case-B footnote identifies the underlying cocontinuous functor).

The compatibilities (lines 1216-1218): a g_n = a_n follows immediately from the definitions - (a g_n)^{-1}G = g_n^{-1}(a^{-1}G) = (a^{-1}G)_n = a_n^{-1}G with all three steps read off the componentwise constructions; item (3) holds because a_*F was defined as the displayed equalizer.
proof_roadmap: Define the component morphisms a_n in both site variants with a_m f_varphi = a_n.
Construct a^{-1} componentwise and a_* as the degree-zero/one equalizer; prove adjointness through the cosimplicial argument.
Read the compatibilities a g_n = a_n and the equalizer formula off the definitions.
difficulty_reason: Structural construction lemma (statement 1140-1159, proof 1161-1233): the augmentation is promoted to a morphism of topoi on the total site by an explicit componentwise construction of a^{-1}, an equalizer definition of a_*, and a cosimplicial adjointness argument (dual of the Simplicial augmentation lemma); the closing compatibilities are definitional with all ingredients in-span, recorded in the notes. H2: construction proof with a cosimplicial bookkeeping finish.
